title: Breaking or Reinforcing the Cycle? Longitudinal Impacts of Bias-Correction Techniques on Feedback Loops and Sustained Financial Inclusion in Machine Learning Credit Scoring
venue: American International Journal of Computer Science and Technology
tldr: Simulates multi-cycle credit scoring to show static fairness interventions backfire over time, while feedback-aware dynamic resampling sustains 18% equity uplift with under 3% default rate increase.
problem_and_motivation: Fairness interventions in ML credit scoring produce unintended long-term effects because models reshape borrower behavior and data iteratively. One-shot fairness evaluations miss feedback loop dynamics that compound disparities.
approach: Simulated 8-12 lending cycles (5-7 years) using 1.2M US loan applications (2018-2024) plus synthetic emerging-market extensions.
Implemented performative prediction framework where decisions reshape future borrower data distributions.
Evaluated adversarial debiasing, pre-processing reweighting, causal proxy mitigation, and threshold adjustments.
Introduced feedback-aware dynamic resampling simulating counterfactual approvals for rejected cases.
Measured demographic parity, AUC-ROC, Brier scores, credit score progression, and inclusion indices.
findings: num: Simple threshold adjustments increased initial Black/Hispanic approvals by 12-15% but widened disparities by 22% in later cycles.
num: Dynamic resampling with feedback-aware modeling sustained 18% equity uplift with less than 3% rise in default rates.
Static fairness fixes trigger reinforcing loops that exacerbate inequalities over time.
Feedback-aware strategies show greater resilience maintaining equitable access without risk escalation.
Performative prediction framework explains why naive debiasing fails under multi-cycle conditions.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Operationalizes performative prediction and feedback loop theory in unified credit scoring simulation. Demonstrates that static fairness interventions inevitably backfire under dynamic lending conditions. Provides empirical evidence that feedback-aware strategies (dynamic resampling) sustain equity gains longer.
directly_justifies: Static debiasing interventions backfire under multi-cycle feedback dynamics.
Dynamic resampling sustains 18% equity uplift vs threshold adjustments.
Feedback loops compound disparities via sampling, feature, and outcome effects.
Performative prediction explains why naive fairness fails in lending.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematically scanned all domains. Assigned 5.B, 5.C, 6.A high for profiling, classification, and prediction. Assigned 14.B medium for deployment. Assigned 8.B low. Rejected non-algorithmic topics as paper is ML-focused.

limitations: Synthetic emerging-market data may not capture all local dynamics.
Limited to XGBoost base classifier; other models may behave differently.
